vn-0tq4.title: Pole: black stickers
vn-0tq4.summary: In the north, poles often have black stickers like Malaysia's, but with a simpler design.

vn-4prs.title: Pole: round concrete, few or no holes
vn-4prs.summary: Round concrete poles normally have many pin holes in the top half. In the north they often have few or none, though pinhole poles do occur there.

vn-6cXr.title: Driving side: right
vn-6cXr.summary: Traffic drives on the right. Cambodia and the Philippines are the only other Southeast Asian countries with normal Street View that also drive on the right.

vn-7U7D.title: Coverage: motorcycle, bone-shaped blur
vn-7U7D.summary: The camera is on a motorbike, so the blur is bone-shaped and higher on one side, sometimes just a helmet. Older Gen 3 and newer Gen 4 both exist. This is the world's biggest motorcycle coverage, so rural motorbike coverage almost surely means here.

vn-7pdd.title: Pole: round concrete, tiny holes on top
vn-7pdd.summary: Round concrete poles with indents and small pin holes near the top are common. Cambodia and Taiwan have the same type.

vn-Bj0v.title: Landscape: clusters of pines on hills
vn-Bj0v.summary: In the far northeast, pine trees (Khasi pines) grow in clusters on hills.

vn-BjVO.title: Direction sign: blue, odd arrows
vn-BjVO.summary: Blue direction signs have a thin white border or none. Their white arrows often point in slightly strange angles instead of straight lines.

vn-C6Qt.title: Route marker: white stone, coloured top
vn-C6Qt.summary: White roadside stones with a red or blue top are common. They show the road number in big print and distances to towns, which helps pinpoint you. Thailand and Cambodia have them too.

vn-EDRU.title: Chevron: black on yellow or white on red
vn-EDRU.summary: Chevron signs are either black on yellow or white on red, and usually show just one arrow.

vn-FGDV.title: Guardrail: red-yellow reflectors
vn-FGDV.summary: A-type guardrails with reflectors that are red on one side and yellow on the other, which is very recognisable.

vn-FORO.title: Landscape: rocky islands from the sea
vn-FORO.summary: On coastal roads east of Hai Phong, many pointy rocky islands rise out of the water.

vn-Fiwd.title: Plate: codes on trucks
vn-Fiwd.summary: Plate codes are often painted on the sides of trucks and other vehicles. They show which region the vehicle is from.

vn-G0Xi.title: Plants: rubber trees with plastic wraps
vn-G0Xi.summary: North of Ho Chi Minh City and in parts of the Central Highlands, rubber trees have thin trunks with plastic wrapped round part of them. They stand in neat dense grids.

vn-JEke.title: Language: many accents on Latin letters
vn-JEke.summary: Vietnamese uses Latin letters with far more accent marks (diacritics) than any other script on Street View. Words are short, usually one syllable.

vn-K108.title: Google car: island, Gen 3, red soil
vn-K108.summary: This southern island near Cambodia only has older Gen 3 coverage (blurrier, softer colours). Look for dark red soil and a big forested ridge to the northeast.

vn-KMuu.title: Pole: thin bamboo poles
vn-KMuu.summary: Thin bamboo poles appear in rural parts of the northwest mountains.

vn-L5FZ.title: Houses: tall, boxy, Greek-style details
vn-L5FZ.summary: In the flat north around Hanoi, houses are tall boxy buildings with many floors and fancy Greek-style pillars and balconies. Similar ones appear near Ho Chi Minh City.

vn-NQ8Q.title: Roads: grain drying on the road
vn-NQ8Q.summary: Grain is often spread out on roads to dry. The Philippines does this too, and Thailand rarely.

vn-QELO.title: Houses: old yellow town buildings
vn-QELO.summary: A historic town just south of Da Nang has old yellow buildings with dark brown doors and details.

vn-RLOA.title: Landscape: dry, sandy and rocky coast
vn-RLOA.summary: On the southern coast northeast of Phan Thiet, the land is dry and sandy, and sometimes very rocky, unlike the rest of the country.

vn-RmGx.title: Pole top: A above the crossbar
vn-RmGx.summary: A pole top shaped like an A sitting on the crossbar is found in the centre of the country.

vn-Rt0w.title: Fences: grid of sticks or bamboo
vn-Rt0w.summary: In the north, fences made from sticks or bamboo in a grid are common. Northeastern India has similar ones.

vn-ShRd.title: Signs: place name prefixes
vn-ShRd.summary: Some place name prefixes, the start of a town name, are typical for certain regions.

vn-V5np.title: Landscape: tourist mountain town
vn-V5np.summary: A tourist town deep in the northern mountains has loads of shop signs and palace-like hotels. The buildings mix a rich European style with a typical Southeast Asian one.

vn-VApw.title: Plants: pepper vines on tree trunks
vn-VApw.summary: Around the Central Highlands, black pepper vines cover tree trunks completely in dense downward-pointing leaves.

vn-VM9t.title: Houses: wooden, on stilts
vn-VM9t.summary: In the northwest, traditional wooden houses stand on stilts, with corrugated metal roofs and triangular openings under the roof edges.

vn-VjVL.title: Sign: yellow-orange background
vn-VjVL.summary: Road signs have a yellow-orange background, which is unique in Southeast Asia.

vn-Vre7.title: Plate: white with black text
vn-Vre7.summary: Licence plates are white with black lettering, in both long and short shapes.

vn-VvpQ.title: Landscape: sand dunes beside the road
vn-VvpQ.summary: A peninsula in the north of Khanh Hoa has many sand dunes next to the road, mostly a divided highway with a smaller paved road for a short stretch.

vn-aaUK.title: Signs: address on storefronts
vn-aaUK.summary: Addresses on shop signs are extremely common and run from house number up to ward, district and province. Look for words like phuong, xa, quan, huyen, tinh and abbreviations such as TP. or H.

vn-aj5h.title: Sign post: red and white stripes
vn-aj5h.summary: Road sign posts are usually painted in red and white stripes.

vn-am6o.title: Landscape: pointy dark rocky mountains
vn-am6o.summary: In the far north, rounded pointy mountains with sparse plants show very dark rock. The wider north has pointy mountains, but bare rock is what sets this area apart.

vn-bsQx.title: Pole: double poles
vn-bsQx.summary: Double poles, in several varieties, are fairly common. Czechia and Slovakia also use paired concrete poles.

vn-bxty.title: Houses: boxy and single-storey
vn-bxty.summary: In the far south, houses are also boxy concrete, but much lower, nearly always one ground floor.

vn-dtNM.title: Landscape: wind turbines
vn-dtNM.summary: Wind turbines sit in a few clusters in the southern half, most often near the coast southeast of Dalat, then north of Buon Ma Thuot and south of Pleiku. A few are offshore south of Ho Chi Minh City.

vn-e8fi.title: Road lines: short yellow dashes
vn-e8fi.summary: Several line types appear, but unusually short yellow centre dashes are very common and distinctive.

vn-eQWy.title: Plants: dragonfruit farms
vn-eQWy.summary: Dragonfruit looks like an upturned wet mop. Farms are in two small southern areas: near Phan Thiet, and on the Long An and Tien Giang border.

vn-fQVL.title: Landscape: greenhouses everywhere
vn-fQVL.summary: Land around Da Lat is densely covered in greenhouses.

vn-fbiz.title: Pole top: crossbar mostly to one side
vn-fbiz.summary: In the south, the crossbar sits clearly to one side, sometimes like Indonesian off-centre poles. If the connector is an incomplete trapezoid, it belongs to a different type.

vn-ir7t.title: Pole: grey meter box with small windows
vn-ir7t.summary: Utility poles often carry light grey electricity boxes with 1 to 4 small indented windows, and the bottom slopes down slightly.

vn-j6ch.title: Landscape: very flat farm fields
vn-j6ch.summary: In the north around Hanoi, and less often in the far south, you see wide, completely flat farm fields.

vn-k87j.title: Pole top: triangle supports
vn-k87j.summary: A triangle of support bars under the crossbar points to the south. The middle insulator must sit on the pole itself, not on an extension of the crossbar.

vn-kRby.title: Coverage: low-quality camera, bone blur
vn-kRby.summary: Some areas use the low-quality shitcam. Its blur matches the motorbike one, unlike the bigger round blur in other countries.

vn-kryK.title: Landscape: lone mountain on a flat plain
vn-kryK.summary: A single big mountain stands in an otherwise flat landscape, just northeast of Tay Ninh.

vn-lm-480351.title: Pole: spools mounted on the pole
vn-lm-480351.summary: Spools fixed straight onto the pole, not on mini bars, are found almost only in the far south.

vn-lm-480352.title: Pole top: half or full trapezoid support
vn-lm-480352.summary: A crossbar with a diagonal support meeting a small horizontal piece below, forming a trapezoid. It can show on both sides or only one half.

vn-lm-480353.title: Pole: plain round concrete
vn-lm-480353.summary: A round concrete pole with no holes. The top does not matter, and it can be doubled. Most common in the north.

vn-lm-480354.hide: no location content, only a cone-shaped animal guard

vn-lm-480355.title: Pole: mini crossbar with spools
vn-lm-480355.summary: Very short L-shaped crossbars with small spools on top. Mostly in the north but they reach far south. In the north they sit on holey poles, in the centre on pinhole poles.

vn-lm-480360.title: Pole: ultra tall, brown band
vn-lm-480360.summary: Very tall poles that look like two stacked, with a small brown section about a third of the way up. Mainly in the north, rarely elsewhere.

vn-lm-480363.title: Pole: lamp mounted far out on bars
vn-lm-480363.summary: A lamp attached to a utility pole by two metal bars, standing well out from the pole. Found in the south, but similar lamps exist.

vn-lm-480367.title: Pole: extended top with metal frame
vn-lm-480367.summary: The pole top is extended with something like a metal frame. Mainly south, but rarely seen anywhere.

vn-lm-480368.title: Pole: silver band
vn-lm-480368.summary: A silver band on the pole, probably an animal guard. Found in the south and rarely in the centre.

vn-lm-483200.title: Phone numbers: start with 02, then area
vn-lm-483200.summary: Numbers start with 0, and a 02 start means a regional number, with 2X or 2XX giving the area. 24 is Hanoi, 28 is Ho Chi Minh City, and codes rise from north to south (29X).

vn-lm-535801.title: Pole: meter box with ventilation slits
vn-lm-535801.summary: Meter boxes with trap-door-style windows and ventilation slits on the sides are very common in Khanh Hoa province, from villages to coast. Other box designs occur everywhere.

vn-lm-535805.title: Landscape: low farmland with canals
vn-lm-535805.summary: Low farmland with some canals is common around Nam Dinh and southern Hanoi. The far south has canals too, but a different landscape.

vn-lm-535810.title: Houses: traditional, north and highlands
vn-lm-535810.summary: Traditional houses are mostly in the north, but also appear in Dak Lak and Gia Lai. The land there is flatter, which helps tell them apart.

vn-nJ04.title: Bollard: white with red top
vn-nJ04.summary: The usual bollard is a small square concrete post painted white with a red top.

vn-noS2.title: Houses: thin spires on roofs
vn-noS2.summary: Thin spires on house roofs are almost only seen in the northern half.

vn-nrTS.title: Vegetation: flat, canals and palms
vn-nrTS.summary: In the far south, the land is very flat and wet, with many straight canals, villages in lines, palm trees and lush wetland plants. Fields are everywhere.

vn-nwf2.title: Pole: concrete with holes
vn-nwf2.summary: Concrete poles with holes either in the lower half or nearly to the top are common. Sri Lanka also has holey poles, but its holes are much bigger.

differs.how: Sri Lankan holes are much larger

vn-oR5n.title: Pole top: upside-down trapezoid
vn-oR5n.summary: Pole tops shaped like an upside-down trapezoid are common. Parts of Sulawesi in Indonesia have similar-looking ones.

vn-opQx.title: Landscape: lone graves in fields
vn-opQx.summary: In the north, single graves stand alone in the middle of farm fields.

vn-quea.title: Pole top: three off-centre trapezoids
vn-quea.summary: If a pole has three off-centre, incomplete trapezoids on its top, you are in the north.

vn-rCnR.title: Coverage: low-quality camera, north
vn-rCnR.summary: The low-quality shitcam appears only in a few spots in the Red River Delta, around Hanoi.

vn-rlN5.title: Barrier: red and white concrete
vn-rlN5.summary: Red and white striped concrete safety barriers are fairly common on mountain roads.

vn-s59g.title: Landscape: red soil and rolling hills
vn-s59g.summary: In the Central Highlands, expect hills, far mountains, red soil and dry, rolling fields. The plants look a bit drier than elsewhere.

vn-sbhF.title: Sign: Russian text beside local text
vn-sbhF.summary: Near the beach resorts east of Phan Thiet, most signs also have Cyrillic text for Russian tourists.

vn-tM34.title: Road surface: concrete block roads
vn-tM34.summary: Small minor roads are often made of concrete blocks. The Philippines and Thailand have them too, Indonesia a bit less.

differs.how: Less common there than in Vietnam

vn-vhPv.title: Pole: holes almost to the top
vn-vhPv.summary: In the north, poles often have holes along most of their length. Do not confuse them with the regular holey pole, where holes stop halfway, which is found countrywide.

vn-whpO.title: Signs: learn the province names
vn-whpO.summary: The province in an address is the most useful part, and is often abbreviated (Tien Giang becomes TG). Provinces were merged in 2025, but most coverage predates that, so learn the old names.

vn-x4O8.title: Plants: trimmed tea bushes
vn-x4O8.summary: Tea fields are mostly in the north, with one big southern area around Bao Loc. They are compact, neatly trimmed dark green bushes, often in curving rows on hillsides.

vn-zI3S.title: Pole top: trapezoid, centre and north
vn-zI3S.summary: Upside-down trapezoid pole tops are common in the central and northern parts. They can be off-centre, which is different from ordinary off-centre poles.
